name: Leon Trotsky
role: Russian revolutionary, Red Army founder and leader of the Left Opposition and Fourth International (1879-1940)
summary: Trotsky was a Marxist revolutionary who helped lead the October Revolution, built the Red Army and, after losing to Stalin, argued that the USSR was a degenerated workers' state needing a political revolution to restore soviet democracy. He championed permanent revolution, internationalism, planned economy and a vanguard party, defended revolutionary violence and dictatorship of the proletariat in the civil war period, and later demanded soviet pluralism and press freedom.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argues socialist planning, not the market, is the road to higher productivity, while acknowledging supply and demand remain a necessary corrective during the transition.

public-ownership.rationale: The Transitional Program demands expropriation of the monopolies holding war industries, railroads and key raw materials, and of the private banks; The Revolution Betrayed defends nationalised property as the gain of October.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Pre-1917 programme work he defends in Results and Prospects/Permanent Revolution calls for a graduated income tax and moving the whole tax burden onto the rich classes.

unions-good.rationale: The Transitional Program says workers need mass trade unions, rebukes ultra-left claims that unions have outlived their usefulness, and requires members to work inside them (while warning they cannot replace the party).

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: he called for expropriating banks, monopolies and landed estates and for abolishing private ownership of the means of production, which rules out treating private property as a near-inviolable right.

strong-leader.rationale: Denounces Stalin's Bonapartist regime, which rises above society and allows no control, as a danger to the revolution.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is a necessary instrument in transition, he argues, but in communism the state and money wither away; he opposed anarchist abolition.

traditional-family.rationale: Describes the traditional family as an 'archaic, stuffy and stagnant institution' and attacks Stalin's cult of the family as serving bureaucratic discipline.

abortion-legal.rationale: Calls the right to abortion one of women's most important civil, political and cultural rights, and attacks Stalin's campaign against it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Calls the League of Nations 'an organization of the violence of the imperialist minority over the overwhelming majority of mankind'.

nation-first.rationale: Proletarian internationalism: rejects national messianism and autarchy, arguing socialism depends on the world division of labour.

revolution-justified.rationale: The central claim of his work: socialist revolution is necessary, and the transitional programme exists to prepare it.

central-planning.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed argues nationalised planned economy has proved its superiority in growth over capitalism, while insisting it needs Soviet democracy and a sound currency to work.

socialized-markets.rationale: In The Revolution Betrayed he says market relations and money must continue through the transitional period between capitalism and socialism, with industry publicly owned.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Supports a democratically controlled national plan that allocates investment and resources through nationalised industry and a single state bank.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Says that in communist society the state and money will wither away, but in the first stage wages by work and money circulation must remain; the abolition is a long-run aim.

one-party-rule.rationale: His mature programme demands legalisation of soviet parties, with workers and peasants freely choosing which parties are soviet; condemned the bureaucratic one-party regime.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: A lifelong opponent of tsarism; his 1905 programme demands a democratic republic based on the sovereignty of the people.

democracy-best.rationale: Rejects the 'deification of democracy' and bourgeois democracy as a class instrument, preferring soviet democracy, though he also defended democratic slogans tactically.

workers-councils.rationale: Calls for soviets as organs of power and for democratising the soviets in the USSR; the Permanent Revolution and Transitional Program rely on soviet power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Called for an independent Soviet Ukraine and defended the right of national separation.

political-violence-never.rationale: Terrorism and Communism and Their Morals and Ours defend revolutionary violence; he rejected the idea that any violence is never justified.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Frames modern history as class struggle (e.g. the proletarian-bourgeois conflict, the Bolshevik tradition), and Marxist materialism as the key to history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Wants 'socialist equality' of distribution to replace bourgeois norms and demands greater equality of wages, abolition of ranks and privileges; the full goal is distribution by need.

direct-action.rationale: Held that power is won by insurrection and soviets rather than by parliamentary majority, but also urged work in trade unions and use of electoral/democratic slogans.

means-match-ends.rationale: Writes that means are subordinated to and interwoven with the end, and that only what leads to human liberation is permissible, rejecting means that set workers against each other.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Endorses Marx's formula 'from each according to his abilities, to each according to his needs' as the communist goal, requiring abundance; the workers' state cannot yet reach it.

production-for-use.rationale: Presents planning in the interest of producers and consumers, and production by social need, against capitalist profit-making.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Uses Marx's account in which capitalists receive surplus value created by workers, and speaks of the 'exorbitant profits of the capitalists'.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Terrorism and Communism defends the dictatorship of the proletariat (with soviet democracy later as its measure) as the only road to abolishing private property.

collective-farming.rationale: Supported gradual, voluntary collectivisation (Lenin's co-operative plan) and condemned Stalin's forced collectivisation and dekulakisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Treats imperialist wars as the product of capitalist productive forces outgrowing the national state, and calls for struggle against imperialism and its wars.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred: he advocated shifting the burden of taxation onto the rich and funding a planned economy by the state.

conscription.rationale: Built the Red Army through mass mobilisation and defended compulsory labour service; the Transitional Program backs military training of workers.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Calls fascist 'race' and 'blood' theories semi-delirious and semi-charlatan.

universal-morality.rationale: Rejects 'eternal moral truths' as an attempt to turn the wheels backward; morality is class-conditioned.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Mixed: said a nation needs a territory and Zionism springs from that, yet held Zionism incapable of resolving the Jewish question and did not believe it could be solved under capitalism and British imperialism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Calls for workers' control of industry via factory committees ('business secrets' opened to workers) and for factory committees to control production in the USSR.

national-self-determination.rationale: Supported independence of Soviet Ukraine and national liberation of colonies as a duty of the international proletariat.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Holds that morality and knowledge move from religion to materialism and criticises appeals to eternal moral truths.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rejects class collaboration and the People's Front, calls Popular Front politics a 'democratic noose' on the proletariat.

workers-nation.rationale: Insists on proletarian internationalism; rejects the national organisation of the working class and 'socialism in one country'.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Describes bourgeois democracy as an instrument adapted to the needs of the ruling classes and the Soviet state, still carrying bourgeois law, as 'guardian of inequality'.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Writes of how 'man enslaved woman' through history and of the toiling woman's 'galley labor', requiring socialisation of housework.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes the Soviet ruling stratum as privileged and cut off from the masses, and capitalist politicians as agents of finance capital.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Inferred: he advocated a state-planned economy with nationalised industry and banking, incompatible with a state limited to defence and justice.

socialism-one-country.rationale: His signature thesis against Stalin: socialism cannot be completed in a single country; it depends on international revolution.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Mocks the bureaucracy's insistence that the state should grow stronger rather than die away, calling it a cult of the bureaucratic state, while accepting the state as necessary during transition.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Rejects absolute prohibitions: means are justified by their end of liberating mankind, and revolution requires force.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Contested: defended banning counter-revolutionary parties in the civil war, but later demanded legalisation of soviet parties and wanted fascism fought by workers' detachments, not state bans.

vanguard-party.rationale: Holds the working class needs a revolutionary vanguard party; unions cannot replace it, and the crisis of mankind is 'the crisis of the revolutionary leadership'.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Defended revolutionary terror and repression as legitimate in civil war against counter-revolution, and rejected abstract legality.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Transitional Program urges committees on prices of delegates from factories, unions, cooperatives and housewives to control prices and counter profiteering, plus a sliding scale of wages.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed attacks the 'heavy muzzle' of censorship held by the Central Committee Secretariat and demands freedom of the press under Soviet democracy.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Cites approvingly payment of officials no higher than a worker's wage as an anti-bureaucratic measure, and attacks the 'party maximum' of the elite.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Transitional Program: in imperialist war 'the chief enemy is in your own country'; defeat of your own imperialist government is the lesser evil.

recall-officials.rationale: Cites the Marx-Engels principle of election and recall at any time as an anti-bureaucratic safeguard.

people-in-arms.rationale: Programme of 1905 demands dissolving the standing army into the armed people and a people's militia; he later built a regular Red Army and criticised its abolition of the militia system.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The theory of permanent revolution holds national emancipation in backward countries is achievable only through proletarian dictatorship and socialist measures.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Mixed: he dissolved the Russian Constituent Assembly as a Bolshevik leader, but in 1938 said the slogan keeps its full force in China and India and for fascist countries.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Examines and rejects the term 'state capitalism' for the USSR, calling it a degenerated workers' state with nationalised property.

leader-cult.rationale: Condemns Stalin's deification, 'Byzantine flattery' and the dogma of infallibility as signs of the regime's decline.

land-redistribution.rationale: Backed peasant seizure of landed estates in 1917 and recognition of the peasants' revolutionary land expropriations; the Transitional Program ties agrarian reform to the revolution in backward countries.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Says the cultural demands of national minorities require the widest possible autonomy, while economy needs central planning.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Contested: argued Zionism cannot solve the Jewish question and urged Jews to join the socialist revolution, while recognising the Jewish nation will persist.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: States that Marxism begins from the development of technique as the fundamental spring of progress and builds the communist programme on the dynamic of productive forces.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Calls autarchy a reactionary defence reflex of senile capitalism and says socialism depends on the world division of labour.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Opposed individual terror and adventurism, wanting insurrection to rest on mass soviet organisation; criticised Comintern 'guerrillaism' and the Canton uprising.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Praises the October Revolution for abolishing privileges, titles and ranks, and demands the abolition of ranks and orders in the USSR.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Transitional Program opens by declaring that capitalism's productive forces have stopped growing and that it is in a 'death agony' that only socialist revolution can resolve.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Calls Stalinism and fascism 'symmetrical' with deadly similarities but rejects equating communism with fascism, which differ in class basis, and rejects 'revolution and reaction are twins'.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Criticises the Soviet campaign against easy divorce and its fees as a retreat to bourgeois law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Cites approvingly the Marx-Engels measures against bureaucracy: election and recall at any time, officials paid no more than a worker.

corporate-influence.rationale: Says '60 Families' dominate US democracy, and the finance-capital cliques of the banks and trusts command the economy and the state.

job-guarantee.rationale: Proposes public works and a sliding scale of working hours so available work is shared among all, including the unemployed, rather than leaving unemployment.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Condemned Stalin's and fascist anti-Semitic scapegoating, which presented internationalists as faithless Jews.

religion-illusion.rationale: Writes that Christianity, like other religions, deadened the consciousness of the oppressed and offered consolation, and that idealism will give way to materialism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Describes classical social democracy as operating in an 'epoch of progressive capitalism', and says capitalism created the world market, division of labour and productive forces that prepare socialism, before it became decadent.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Argues the state cannot give women equality simply by law: equality requires socialised child-rearing and a developed economy.

socialized-care.rationale: Argued the 'family hearth' should be replaced by creches, kindergartens, social dining rooms and laundries, and that returning to home cooking means 'the old slavery'.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Contested: he defended banning opposition parties in the civil war (and suppressed Kronstadt) as episodic self-defence, but in his mature programme demanded freedom for soviet parties and criticised the regime of suppression.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Argues the '60 families' of the United States and '200 families' of France dominate democracy and calls for their expropriation.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Dismisses the principle of the 'sacredness of human life' as a lie while society is based on exploitation, and rejects absolute pacifism as a moral doctrine.

independent-unions.rationale: Fights any attempt to subordinate unions to the bourgeois state and demands the freedom of trade unions from the Soviet bureaucracy.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Argues the USSR is not socialist because the bureaucracy rules, and calls for a political revolution restoring soviet democracy.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Demands complete abolition of secret diplomacy and publication of all treaties and the Kremlin's diplomatic correspondence.

workers-own-party.rationale: Founded the Fourth International to build independent revolutionary workers' parties and rejects subordinating workers to bourgeois parties.

women-suffrage.rationale: Praises the October Revolution for giving women full political and legal rights in equality with men.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Held the USSR a degenerated workers' state to be defended against imperialism and capitalist restoration despite the bureaucracy.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Uses the Marxian surplus-value analysis (value and profit arising from labour) when describing capitalist and Soviet economies.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Defended the NEP (a state-supervised market under Bolshevik rule) as necessary; criticised Stalin's abandonment of it as adventurism, though he stressed Soviet democracy as the real corrective.

notes: Positions shifted from the civil war (banning rival parties, compulsory labour, terror) to a 1930s programme of soviet pluralism and press freedom; the latter is used where they conflict. Not covered by his available writings: LGBT issues, drugs, environment, healthcare provision and most modern policy questions, which stay null.
